topics.title: Regular Polygons and Nested Radicals
topics.subtitle: Archimedean Edge-Doubling Recursion, Golden Decagon/Pentagon Radicals, and the Pentadecagon
topics.enunciation: For a regular N-gon inscribed in a unit circle (R = 1), doubling the number of sides maps edge length E_{N/2} to E_N = sqrt(2 - sqrt(4 - E_{N/2}^2)), generating closed-form nested quadratic radicals for the 2^k, 3*2^k, 5*2^k, and 15*2^k polygon families.
synthesis: Spanning 18 folios (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig's treatise on regular :term:`polygons` derives the Archimedean edge-doubling recursion :math:`E_N = \sqrt{2 - \sqrt{4 - E_{N/2}^2}}` (for circumradius :math:`R=1`, where :math:`E_N = 2\sin(\pi/N)` and apothem :math:`r_N = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4 - E_N^2}`) and compiles complete nested-radical tables across four constructible families: the square/octagon chain (:math:`E_4 = \sqrt{2}, E_8 = \sqrt{2-\sqrt{2}}, E_{16}, E_{32}, E_{64}`), the triangle/hexagon/dodecagon chain (:math:`E_3 = \sqrt{3}, E_6 = 1, E_{12} = \sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}, E_{24}`), and the :term:`golden ratio` pentagon/decagon chain (:math:`E_5 = \sqrt{3-\phi} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{10-2\sqrt{5}} \approx 1.17557, E_{10} = \sqrt{2-\phi} = \phi - 1 \approx 0.61803, E_{20} = \sqrt{2-\sqrt{2+\phi}}`).

Dated April 20, 2015, the second half of the dossier investigates the regular 15-gon (:person:`Euclid` *Elements* :ref:`IV.16`, :math:`E_{15} = 2\sin 12^\circ \approx 0.41582`), citing James Stafford's exact radical table for multiples of :math:`\pi/30 = 6^\circ`, alongside an angle-chasing exploration of the regular enneagon (:math:`N=9`, requiring a cubic trisection) and two auxiliary Cartesian cevian sheets.
equations: E_N = 2\sin\frac{\pi}{N} = \sqrt{2 - \sqrt{4 - E_{N/2}^2}}, \qquad r_N = \cos\frac{\pi}{N} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4 - E_N^2}
E_{10} = \phi - 1 = \sqrt{2 - \phi}, \qquad E_5 = \sqrt{3 - \phi}, \qquad E_{15} = 2\sin 12^\circ = \frac{1}{4}\left(\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}} + \sqrt{3} - \sqrt{15}\right)
folio_summaries: Edge-Doubling Recursion for Unit-Circle Polygons (2-001)
Derives :math:`E_N = \sqrt{2-\sqrt{4-E_{N/2}^2}}` and apothem :math:`r_N = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4-E_N^2}` from the sagitta right triangle in a unit circle (:math:`R=1`).
Square & Octagon Doubling Family (2-002)
Evaluates nested radicals for :math:`N = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64` starting from :math:`E_4 = \sqrt{2}`.
Hexagon & Dodecagon Doubling Family (2-003)
Evaluates nested radicals for :math:`N = 3, 6, 12, 24, 48` starting from :math:`E_3 = \sqrt{3}` and :math:`E_6 = 1`.
Pentagon & Decagon Golden Ratio Radicals (2-004)
Expresses :math:`E_{10} = \phi^{-1} = \sqrt{2-\phi}`, :math:`E_5 = \sqrt{3-\phi}`, and :math:`E_{20} = \sqrt{2-\sqrt{2+\phi}}` in terms of :math:`\phi = \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}`.
Master Polygon Reference Table (2-005)
Compiles :math:`N, \theta_N, E_N, r_N`, and perimeter :math:`N E_N \to 2\pi` across all constructible families.
Regular Pentadecagon E_15 Derivation (2-006, FWS 4/20/2015)
Computes :math:`E_{15} = 2\sin 12^\circ \approx 0.415823` using :math:`12^\circ = 30^\circ - 18^\circ` and Euclid IV.16.
Stafford's Exact Radical Table for pi/30 (2-007)
Cites James Stafford's trigonometric radical table for multiples of :math:`6^\circ = \pi/30` to verify :math:`\sin 12^\circ` and :math:`\cos 12^\circ`.
Pentadecagon Apothem & Area (2-008)
Simplifies the nested radical for :math:`r_{15} = \cos 12^\circ` and the area :math:`K_{15} = \frac{15}{2}E_{15}r_{15}`.
30-gon & 60-gon Doubling Steps (2-009)
Applies the edge-doubling recursion to :math:`E_{15}` to obtain :math:`E_{30}` and :math:`E_{60}`.
Inscribed Triangle & Square Constructions (001)
Compass diagrams of the inscribed equilateral triangle (:math:`E_3 = \sqrt{3}R`) and square (:math:`E_4 = \sqrt{2}R`).
Inscribed Pentagon & Decagon Geometry (002)
Shows Ptolemy's / Euclid XIII.10 relation :math:`E_5^2 = R^2 + E_{10}^2` inside the unit circle.
Golden Triangle & Gnomon Decomposition of the Decagon (003)
Partitions the regular decagon into ten acute :math:`72^\circ\text{--}72^\circ\text{--}36^\circ` golden triangles.
Chord Length & Central Angle Identities (004)
Relates chord length :math:`c(\theta) = 2R\sin(\theta/2)` to the sagitta :math:`s = R - \sqrt{R^2 - (c/2)^2}`.
Polygon Perimeter & Area Convergence to pi (005)
Tabulates :math:`\pi_N = \frac{N}{2}E_N` and :math:`A_N = \frac{N}{2}E_N r_N` for increasing :math:`N`.
Regular Enneagon (N = 9) Angle-Chasing Attempt — Page 1 (006)
Investigates chord relationships in the regular 9-gon (:math:`20^\circ` central half-angle).
Regular Enneagon (N = 9) Diagonal Relations — Page 2 (007)
Records the three diagonal lengths of the regular enneagon and notes the irreducible cubic :math:`x^3 - 3x + 1 = 0`.
Cartesian Cevian Length Sheet — Part 1 (009)
Derives cevian segment lengths in a Cartesian triangle frame.
Cartesian Cevian Length Sheet — Part 2 (010)
Completes the algebraic expansion of the Cartesian cevian length formula.

topics.title: Geometric Problems and Extremal Loci
topics.subtitle: Maximizing Euler Distance d_IO for Acute Triangles, Monte Carlo Vesica Integration, and 25-Problem Compendium
topics.enunciation: Among all triangles with longest side c = |AB| = 1, the acute locus inside the vesica piscis above the semicircle on AB has area A = int_0^{sqrt(3)} (sqrt(4 - x^2) - 1) dx - pi/4 = (5 pi - 6 sqrt(3))/12 approx 0.44297 (for c = 2), and maximizing d_IO over acute triangles approaches the degenerate right-isosceles limit C -> (0, 1).
synthesis: This 10-folio collection (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`) combines two analytic geometry sheets (Folios 1–2), a dated calculus and Monte Carlo investigation *Find an acute triangle that maximizes :math:`d_{IO}`* (`FWS 2015/04/24`, Folios 3–4), and a 25-problem compendium (*Problem Set*, Folios 5–10) that served as the blueprint for Seelig's notebook archive.

In his April 24, 2015 study, Seelig fixes base :math:`c = 2` and constrains vertex :g:`C` to the region where :math:`c` is the longest side (inside the :term:`vesica piscis` of radii 2 centered at :g:`A` and :g:`B`) while :math:`\triangle ABC` remains acute (outside the semicircle :g:`c_semi` of radius 1 and between the vertical lines at :g:`A` and :g:`B`). Integrating :math:`A = \int_0^{\sqrt{3}}(\sqrt{4-x^2}-1)\,dx - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{5\pi - 6\sqrt{3}}{12} \approx 0.44297`, he explains why his spreadsheet Monte Carlo sampler on :math:`[0,\sqrt{3}]\times[0,1]` has an acceptance rate of :math:`0.44297/\sqrt{3} \approx 25.6\%`, and finds that :math:`d_{IO}` increases monotonically toward the right-triangle boundary :math:`C \to (0, 1)`.
equations: A_{\text{acute}} = \int_0^{\sqrt{3}} \left(\sqrt{4 - x^2} - 1\right) dx - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{5\pi - 6\sqrt{3}}{12} \approx 0.44297
p_{\text{accept}} = \frac{A_{\text{acute}}}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 0.25575, \qquad d_{IO} = \sqrt{R^2 - 2 r R}

topics.title: Altitude of a Pythagorean Triple Triangle
topics.subtitle: Inverse Pythagorean Theorem, Hypotenuse Projections, and Incircle Touchpoint Distinction
topics.enunciation: In a right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c, the altitude h_c = a b / c satisfies the Inverse Pythagorean Theorem 1/h_c^2 = 1/a^2 + 1/b^2 and divides the hypotenuse into projections u = b^2/c and y = a^2/c with h_c^2 = u y.
synthesis: Titled *The Altitude of a Pythagorean Triple Triangle* (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), this four-folio study examines the right-triangle altitude :g:`h_c` dropped from the right angle :g:`C` to the hypotenuse :g:`A` :g:`B` (:person:`Euclid` *Elements* :ref:`VI.8`). Equating twice the area :math:`2K = ab = ch_c` gives :math:`h_c = ab/c` and the Inverse Pythagorean Theorem :math:`\frac{1}{h_c^2} = \frac{a^2+b^2}{a^2 b^2} = \frac{1}{a^2} + \frac{1}{b^2}`, while the hypotenuse projections :math:`u = b^2/c` and :math:`y = a^2/c` satisfy the :term:`geometric mean` identity :math:`h_c = \sqrt{uy}`.

On Folio 3, Seelig highlights a classic geometric pitfall inside a bold warning box: the cevian from :g:`C` to the :term:`incircle` touchpoint :g:`T_C` (which splits :math:`c` into :math:`s-a` and :math:`s-b` with :math:`K = (s-a)(s-b)`) does *not* coincide with the perpendicular altitude foot :g:`H_C` (*"CT_c is not \perp to BA"*) unless :math:`a = b`.
equations: h_c = \frac{a b}{c}, \qquad \frac{1}{h_c^2} = \frac{1}{a^2} + \frac{1}{b^2}, \qquad u = \frac{b^2}{c},\; y = \frac{a^2}{c},\; h_c^2 = u y
|A T_C| = s - a \neq u = \frac{b^2}{c} \quad (a \neq b), \qquad K = (s - a)(s - b) = \frac{a b}{2}
folio_summaries: Altitude of a Pythagorean Triple Triangle (001)
Derives :math:`h_c = ab/c`, the Inverse Pythagorean Theorem :math:`h_c^{-2} = a^{-2} + b^{-2}`, and the hypotenuse segments :math:`u = b^2/c, y = a^2/c`.

Orthocentric Projection Segments (004)
Relates the right-triangle altitude segments to the general orthocentric system of an acute/obtuse triangle.

topics.title: Radical Axes and Radical Center
topics.subtitle: Two-Circle Radical Division, Vertex-Altitude Circle Radical Center, and Circular Lens Regimes
topics.enunciation: The radical axis of two circles of radii r_1, r_2 with center separation d cuts the line of centers at x = d/2 + (r_1^2 - r_2^2)/(2 d) from O_1, and the three radical axes of the vertex-altitude circles Gamma_A(h_A), Gamma_B(h_B), Gamma_C(h_C) concur at the radical center W.
synthesis: Spanning 11 folios (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig's treatise on the :term:`radical axis` begins (Folio 1) with the fundamental two-circle division formula :math:`x = \frac{d}{2} + \frac{r_1^2 - r_2^2}{2d}`, tested on :math:`r_1=1, r_2=2, d=5` to give :math:`|O_1 P| = 2.2, |O_2 P| = 2.8`, and equal tangent length :math:`t = \frac{4\sqrt{6}}{5} \approx 1.9596`. Folios 2–8 (`FWS Dec. 8/2014`) execute an ambitious 7-page analytic calculation: placing circles :math:`\Gamma_A(h_A), \Gamma_B(h_B), \Gamma_C(h_C)` at the vertices of a triangle with radii equal to the three altitudes, Seelig derives each pairwise radical axis in double-intercept form :math:`\frac{x}{x_0} + \frac{y}{y_0} = 1` and solves for their common :term:`radical center` :math:`W = (2.586, 0.603)` on the :math:`(2,3,4)` triangle.

Folios 9–11 classify the five relative position regimes of two circles as :math:`d` varies from :math:`d > r_1 + r_2` (disjoint) through external/internal tangency to :math:`d < |r_1 - r_2|`, recording the circular lens intersection chord and area.
equations: \Gamma_A(A, h_A),\; \Gamma_B(B, h_B),\; \Gamma_C(C, h_C) \implies \frac{x}{x_0} + \frac{y}{y_0} = 1
folio_summaries: Two-Circle Radical Axis & Equal Tangents (001)
Derives :math:`x = \frac{d}{2} + \frac{r_1^2-r_2^2}{2d}` and tests :math:`r_1=1, r_2=2, d=5 \implies x=2.2, x'=2.8, t = \frac{4\sqrt{6}}{5}`.
Radical Center of Vertex-Altitude Circles — Setup (002, FWS Dec. 8/2014)
Defines circles :math:`\Gamma_A(h_A), \Gamma_B(h_B), \Gamma_C(h_C)` centered at :math:`A, B, C` with radii equal to the three altitudes.
Radical Axis of Gamma_A and Gamma_B (003)
Computes the radical foot along side :math:`c = AB` and writes the perpendicular line equation.
Radical Axis of Gamma_A and Gamma_C in Intercept Form (004)
Projects the radical axis of :math:`\Gamma_A` and :math:`\Gamma_C` onto the Cartesian frame of :math:`AB` and derives :math:`x/x_0 + y/y_0 = 1`.
Radical Axis of Gamma_B and Gamma_C (005)
Derives the double-intercept equation for the third radical axis opposite side :math:`a = BC`.
2x2 Linear System for the Radical Center W (006)
Intersects two radical axes in intercept form to solve for the radical center :math:`W = (W_x, W_y)`.
Numerical Evaluation on the (2, 3, 4) Triangle — Part 1 (007)
Computes the altitudes :math:`h_A, h_B, h_C` and pairwise radical intercepts of the :math:`(2,3,4)` obtuse triangle.
Numerical Evaluation on the (2, 3, 4) Triangle — Part 2 (008)
Finds the exact radical center coordinates :math:`W = (2.586, 0.603)` and verifies concurrency of all three radical axes.
Two-Circle Separation Regimes (009)
Classifies disjoint, externally tangent, intersecting, internally tangent, and nested circle pairs by comparing :math:`d` with :math:`r_1 \pm r_2`.
Common Chord & Sagitta of Intersecting Circles (010)
Expresses the common chord length :math:`2y = 2\sqrt{r_1^2 - x^2}` in terms of Heron's radical on :math:`(r_1, r_2, d)`.
Circular Lens Area Formula (011)
Integrates/sums the two circular sector-minus-triangle segments to obtain the asymmetric lens area.

folios.heading: Two-Circle Radical Axis & Equal Tangents (001)
folios.diplomatic_rst:
**Diplomatic Transcription — Folio 0271** (``0271.jpg``, Sheet 1 of 11):

topics.title: Homothetic Ratios and Crossed Diagonals
topics.subtitle: Internal and External Division of Parallel Uprights from a Center of Similitude
topics.enunciation: Given two parallel uprights of heights h_1 < h_2 separated by horizontal distance d and viewed from their external center of similitude O, the crossed diagonals meet at horizontal distance x = d h_1 / (h_1 + h_2) from the first upright, while O lies at distance y - x = d h_1 / (h_2 - h_1) to its left, forming a harmonic range.
synthesis: Across five folios (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig analyzes the projective and metric proportions of two homothetic right triangles sharing an apex angle :math:`\phi` at :g:`O_ext` with parallel vertical uprights :math:`h_1 < h_2` separated by distance :math:`d` along the baseline :g:`A` :g:`B`. By similar triangles (:person:`Euclid` *Elements* :ref:`VI.2` and :ref:`VI.4`), the crossed diagonals :math:`AP_2` and :math:`BP_1` intersect at :g:`O_int` at horizontal distance :math:`x = d\frac{h_1}{h_1+h_2}` from :g:`A` (and height :math:`h = \frac{h_1 h_2}{h_1+h_2}`, half the :term:`harmonic mean`), while the external apex :g:`O_ext` lies at distance :math:`y - x = d\frac{h_1}{h_2-h_1}` from :g:`A`.

Adding the internal and external distances yields the total span between the two centers of similitude :math:`y = \frac{2 d h_1 h_2}{h_2^2 - h_1^2}` and its midpoint :math:`z = \frac{d h_1 h_2}{h_2^2 - h_1^2}`, reproducing the Apollonian :term:`harmonic conjugate` formulas with :math:`k = h_2/h_1`.
equations: x = d\frac{h_1}{h_1 + h_2}, \qquad y - x = d\frac{h_1}{h_2 - h_1}, \qquad h = \frac{h_1 h_2}{h_1 + h_2}
folio_summaries: Homothetic Right Triangles & Crossed Diagonals (001)
Sets up uprights :math:`h_1, h_2` separated by :math:`d` from apex :math:`O` (angle :math:`\phi`) and derives :math:`x = d h_1/(h_1+h_2)` and :math:`y-x = d h_1/(h_2-h_1)`.
Total Span y & Midpoint z Between Similitude Centers (002)
Combines :math:`x` and :math:`y-x` to obtain :math:`y = \frac{2dh_1h_2}{h_2^2-h_1^2}` and :math:`z = \frac{dh_1h_2}{h_2^2-h_1^2}`.
Crossed-Ladder Height & Harmonic Mean (003)
Shows that the height of the crossed-diagonal intersection is :math:`h = \frac{h_1 h_2}{h_1+h_2} = \frac{1}{2}H(h_1,h_2)`, independent of :math:`d`.
Dimensionless Ratio Parameterization k = h_2 / h_1 (004)
Divides top and bottom by :math:`h_1^2` to recover the canonical Apollonian formulas :math:`x = d/(k+1), y-x = d/(k-1), z = dk/(k^2-1)`.
Numerical & Graphical Verification (005)
Tests the formulas on integer height pairs :math:`(h_1, h_2) = (1,2)` and :math:`(2,3)`.

folios.heading: Homothetic Right Triangles & Crossed Diagonals (001)
folios.diplomatic_rst:
**Diplomatic Transcription — Folio 0282** (``0282.jpg``, Sheet 1 of 5):

Sets up uprights :math:`h_1, h_2` separated by :math:`d` from apex :math:`O` (angle :math:`\phi`) and derives :math:`x = d h_1/(h_1+h_2)` and :math:`y-x = d h_1/(h_2-h_1)`.

.. math::

   x = d\frac{h_1}{h_1 + h_2}, \qquad y - x = d\frac{h_1}{h_2 - h_1}, \qquad h = \frac{h_1 h_2}{h_1 + h_2}
folios.notes_rst: Archival scan ``0282.jpg`` from Fred W. Seelig's notebook dossier on **F.44 Homothetic Ratios and Crossed Diagonals** (Page 1 of 5). Companion OpenDocument worksheet(s): ``Centers of Similitude``, ``Harmonic Conjugates``. Classical Euclidean foundations: :ref:`VI.2`, :ref:`VI.4`.

folios.heading: Total Span y & Midpoint z Between Similitude Centers (002)
folios.diplomatic_rst:
**Diplomatic Transcription — Folio 0283** (``0283.jpg``, Sheet 2 of 5):

Combines :math:`x` and :math:`y-x` to obtain :math:`y = \frac{2dh_1h_2}{h_2^2-h_1^2}` and :math:`z = \frac{dh_1h_2}{h_2^2-h_1^2}`.

.. math::

   y = \frac{2 d h_1 h_2}{h_2^2 - h_1^2}, \qquad z = \frac{y}{2} = \frac{d h_1 h_2}{h_2^2 - h_1^2}
folios.notes_rst: Archival scan ``0283.jpg`` from Fred W. Seelig's notebook dossier on **F.44 Homothetic Ratios and Crossed Diagonals** (Page 2 of 5). Companion OpenDocument worksheet(s): ``Centers of Similitude``, ``Harmonic Conjugates``. Classical Euclidean foundations: :ref:`VI.2`, :ref:`VI.4`.

folios.diplomatic_rst:
**Diplomatic Transcription — Folio 0284** (``0284.jpg``, Sheet 3 of 5):

Shows that the height of the crossed-diagonal intersection is :math:`h = \frac{h_1 h_2}{h_1+h_2} = \frac{1}{2}H(h_1,h_2)`, independent of :math:`d`.

.. math::

   x = d\frac{h_1}{h_1 + h_2}, \qquad y - x = d\frac{h_1}{h_2 - h_1}, \qquad h = \frac{h_1 h_2}{h_1 + h_2}

topics.title: Squares, Subdivided Lattices, and the Japanese Theorem
topics.subtitle: Inscribed Squares, Cevians Inside a Square, Equilateral Subdivisions, and Carnot's Theorem
topics.enunciation: A square inscribed in a circle of radius R has side s = sqrt(2) R; inside a square of side s, intersecting cevians divide the interior in exact rational proportions, and by Carnot's Theorem the sum of inradii in any triangulation of a cyclic polygon is invariant.
synthesis: This six-folio compilation (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`) brings together four geometric studies centered on regular :term:`polygons` and triangulations: Folio 1 pairs the compass construction of a square (:math:`s = \sqrt{2}R`) and an :term:`equilateral triangle` (:math:`s = \sqrt{3}R`) inscribed in a circle of radius :math:`R`; Folios 2–3 solve for the Cartesian intersection :math:`N = (X_N, Y_N)` of two diagonal/edge cevians inside a square of side :math:`s`; Folio 4–5 analyze subdivided equilateral triangle lattices of side 6 and side 1; and Folio 6 summarizes :person:`Carnot`'s Theorem (:math:`OM_A + OM_B + OM_C = R + r`) as the foundation of the classic Japanese Sangaku theorem on cyclic polygon triangulations.
equations: s_{\square} = \sqrt{2}\,R, \qquad s_{\triangle} = \sqrt{3}\,R, \qquad OM_A + OM_B + OM_C = R + r
X_N = \frac{s \cdot u v}{u + v - u v}, \qquad Y_N = \frac{s \cdot u (1 - v)}{u + v - u v}

topics.title: Stewart's Theorem
topics.subtitle: Cevian Length Identity f^2 = k a^2 + k' b^2 - k k' c^2 and Apollonius's Median Formula
topics.enunciation: If a cevian of length f from C divides base c = AB into segments k' c and k c (with k + k' = 1), Stewart's Theorem states f^2 = k a^2 + k' b^2 - k k' c^2; at the midpoint k = k' = 1/2, this yields Apollonius's median formula f^2 = (1/2)(a^2 + b^2 - c^2/2).
synthesis: Dated November 18, 2013 (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig's two-page proof of :term:`Stewart's theorem` (*"Stewart's Theorem (also called :person:`Apollonius`' Theorem)"*, after :person:`Stewart`'s 1746 *Some General Theorems of Considerable Use in the Higher Parts of Mathematics*, :cite:`Stewart1746`) normalizes the base segments of :math:`c = AB` by dimensionless barycentric weights :math:`k' = |AD|/c` and :math:`k = |DB|/c` (:math:`k + k' = 1`). Applying the Law of Cosines (or Euclid II.12/II.13 via the altitude foot :g:`H_C`) to the supplementary angles at :g:`D`, the cosine terms cancel upon weighting by :math:`k` and :math:`k'`, leaving the universal cevian formula :math:`f^2 = k a^2 + k' b^2 - k k' c^2`.

On Folio 2, Seelig sets :math:`k = k' = 1/2` to immediately recover Apollonius's median length identity :math:`m_c^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(a^2 + b^2 - \frac{1}{2}c^2\right)`. On the canonical :math:`(5,6,7)` triangle, this gives :math:`m_c^2 = \frac{1}{2}(25 + 36 - 49/2) = \frac{73}{4}`, so :math:`m_c = \frac{\sqrt{73}}{2}`.
equations: f^2 = k a^2 + k' b^2 - k k' c^2 \qquad (k + k' = 1,\; |AD| = k' c,\; |DB| = k c)
k = k' = \frac{1}{2} \implies m_c^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(a^2 + b^2 - \frac{1}{2}c^2\right) = \frac{2 a^2 + 2 b^2 - c^2}{4}
folio_summaries: Stewart's Theorem Proof (stewart-001, FWS 11/18/2013)

Defines dimensionless base fractions :math:`k, k'` (:math:`k+k'=1`) for cevian :math:`f = |CD|` and eliminates :math:`\cos\theta` between :math:`\triangle ACD` and :math:`\triangle BCD` to prove :math:`f^2 = k a^2 + k' b^2 - k k' c^2`.
Apollonius's Median Formula as Special Case (stewart-002)
Evaluates Stewart's identity at the midpoint :math:`k = k' = 1/2` to obtain :math:`f^2 = \frac{1}{2}(a^2 + b^2 - \frac{1}{2}c^2)`.

topics.title: The UVW Coordinate Triangle
topics.subtitle: Altitude-Origin Cartesian Frame A(-U,0), B(W,0), C(0,V) and 2x2 Cevian Trace Matrices
topics.enunciation: Placing the altitude foot H_C at the origin (0, 0) with A = (-U, 0), B = (W, 0), and C = (0, V) parameterizes any triangle by three numbers (U, V, W) with a = sqrt(V^2 + W^2), b = sqrt(U^2 + V^2), c = U + W, and reduces the cevian traces D, E, F through P(p, q) to explicit 2x2 rational matrix formulas.
synthesis: Across 11 folios (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig develops his signature coordinate apparatus: *The UVW Triangle*. By placing the altitude foot :g:`H_C` at the Cartesian origin :math:`(0,0)` so that :g:`A` :math:`= (-U, 0)`, :g:`B` :math:`= (W, 0)`, and :g:`C` :math:`= (0, V)`, every side and line equation enters double-intercept form (:math:`AC: -x/U + y/V = 1` and :math:`BC: x/W + y/V = 1`). When :math:`(U, V)` and :math:`(V, W)` are chosen as legs of two Pythagorean triples sharing height :math:`V`—such as :math:`(U,V,W) = (5,12,16)` on Folios 3–4—the juxtaposed triangle has integer sides :math:`(a,b,c) = (20, 13, 21)` and integer area :math:`K = 126` (a Heronian triangle).

Given an interior perspector :g:`P` :math:`= (p, q)`, Seelig formulates :math:`2\times 2` matrix systems for the cevian traces :g:`D` :math:`= BC \cap AP`, :g:`E` :math:`= CA \cap BP`, and :g:`F` :math:`= AB \cap CP`, testing the formulas on :math:`(U,V,W,p,q) = (8,8,16,4,4)` to obtain exact rational traces :math:`D = (6.4, 4.8), E = (-2, 6), F = (8, 0)` and verifying :person:`Ceva`'s ratio product :math:`1`.
equations: F_x = \frac{p V}{V - q}, \qquad D = \left(\frac{W V (U + p)}{V(U + W) + q W},\; \frac{V q (U + W)}{V(U + W) + q W}\right)
folio_summaries: The UVW Triangle — Coordinate & Intercept Setup (001)
Places :math:`A=(-U,0), B=(W,0), C=(0,V)` around the altitude foot :math:`(0,0)` and writes the intercept equations of sides :math:`AC` and :math:`BC`.
2x2 Matrix System for Cevian Trace D (002)
Intersects line :math:`AP` through :math:`P(p,q)` with side :math:`BC` via Cramer's rule to solve for :math:`D = (D_x, D_y)`.
Heronian Juxtaposition Example (U, V, W) = (5, 12, 16) — Page 1 (003)
Combines :math:`(5,12,13)` and :math:`(12,16,20)` along shared altitude :math:`V=12` to form the :math:`(20,13,21)` Heronian triangle (:math:`K=126`).
Heronian Juxtaposition Example — Centers & Radii (004)
Computes :math:`s=27, r = 14/3, R = 65/6`, and the coordinates of :math:`G, I, O, H` in the :math:`(5,12,16)` UVW frame.
2x2 Matrix System for Cevian Trace E (005)
Intersects line :math:`BP` with side :math:`AC` to derive the closed-form coordinates of :math:`E = (E_x, E_y)`.
Cevian Trace F on the Baseline & Ceva Ratios (006)
Finds :math:`F = (pV/(V-q), 0)` on the :math:`x`-axis and computes the signed Ceva ratios along all three sides.
Worked Benchmark (U, V, W, p, q) = (8, 8, 16, 4, 4) — Page 1 (007)
Evaluates the matrix formulas at :math:`U=8, V=8, W=16, P=(4,4)` to obtain :math:`D=(6.4, 4.8), E=(-2, 6), F=(8, 0)`.
Worked Benchmark (8, 8, 16, 4, 4) — Ceva & Menelaus Check (008)
Verifies that the segment ratios determined by :math:`D, E, F` multiply to :math:`1`.
Barycentric Conversion in the UVW Frame (009)
Expresses the normalized barycentric coordinates :math:`(\lambda_A, \lambda_B, \lambda_C)` of :math:`P(p,q)` in terms of :math:`U, V, W`.
Inverse Mapping from (a, b, c) to (U, V, W) (010)
Uses Euclid II.12/II.13 to recover :math:`U = (b^2+c^2-a^2)/(2c), W = (a^2+c^2-b^2)/(2c)`, and :math:`V = 2K/c`.

Summarizes the cell formulas implemented in the ``UVW Triangle`` tab of ``Triangles and Circles.ods``.

topics.title: Verisimilitude, Corner Subtriangles, and Excircle Homothety
topics.subtitle: Incircle Tangent Subtriangles (r_A + r_B + r_C = r), Excircle Similitude, and Cevian Bounds
topics.enunciation: If lines parallel to the sides of triangle ABC are drawn tangent to the incircle, the three corner subtriangles are homothetic to ABC with scale factors x/s, y/s, z/s (where x = s - a, y = s - b, z = s - c), so their inradii satisfy r_A + r_B + r_C = r.
synthesis: In this nine-folio investigation (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig explores homothetic scaling (*verisimilitude*) across three connected settings. First (Folios 1–4), drawing tangents to the :term:`incircle` parallel to :math:`BC, CA, AB` cuts off three corner subtriangles homothetic to :math:`\triangle ABC` from vertices :g:`A`, :g:`B`, :g:`C`. Because the distance from :g:`A` to the incircle touchpoint is :math:`x = s-a`, the corner subtriangle at :g:`A` has semiperimeter :math:`s_A = x = s-a`! Consequently its scale factor is :math:`x/s`, its inradius is :math:`r_A = r(x/s)`, its area is :math:`K_A = K(x/s)^2`, and summing over all three corners gives the remarkable invariant :math:`r_A + r_B + r_C = r\frac{x+y+z}{s} = r`.

Second (`FWS 2014/9/7`, Folios 5–6), Seelig analyzes *CENTERS OF SIMILITUDE: EXCIRCLES*, treating vertex :g:`A` as the external :term:`center of similitude` of the incircle :math:`(I, r)` and the :math:`A`-excircle :math:`(I_A, R_A)` separated by :math:`d = |II_A|`, deriving :math:`|AI| = d\frac{r}{R_A - r}` and :math:`|AI_A| = d\frac{R_A}{R_A - r}`. Third (Folios 7–9), he solves :term:`Stewart's theorem` as a quadratic in :math:`k` for a prescribed cevian length :math:`d = 4` in :math:`(a,b,c) = (7,5,10)`, finding the two roots :math:`k \in \{0.613, 0.147\}` above the altitude minimum :math:`d_{\min} = h_c = 3.25`.
equations: s_A = x = s - a, \qquad r_A = r\frac{x}{s}, \qquad K_A = K\left(\frac{x}{s}\right)^2, \qquad r_A + r_B + r_C = r\frac{x + y + z}{s} = r
|AI| = |II_A|\frac{r}{r_a - r}, \qquad |AI_A| = |II_A|\frac{r_a}{r_a - r}, \qquad c^2 k^2 - (c^2 + a^2 - b^2) k + (a^2 - d^2) = 0
folio_summaries: Corner Subtriangles Tangent to the Incircle — Semiperimeter s_A = x (001)
Proves by equal tangent segments that the corner subtriangle cut off at vertex :math:`A` by a tangent to the incircle parallel to :math:`BC` has semiperimeter :math:`s_A = s - a = x`.
Inradii Sum Identity r_A + r_B + r_C = r (002)
Uses homothety ratio :math:`x/s` to derive :math:`r_A = r(x/s), K_A = K(x/s)^2`, and :math:`r_A + r_B + r_C = r(x+y+z)/s = r`.
Infinite Chain of Tangential Corner Incircles (003)
Sums the geometric series of nested incircles marching into vertex :math:`A` with ratio :math:`\rho_A = (1 - \sin(\alpha/2))/(1 + \sin(\alpha/2))`.
Numerical Evaluation on the (5, 6, 7) Triangle (004)
Evaluates :math:`x/s = 4/9, y/s = 3/9, z/s = 2/9` and checks :math:`r_A + r_B + r_C = r` and :math:`K_A + K_B + K_C = \frac{29}{81}K`.
Centers of Similitude: Excircles — Part 1 (005, FWS 2014/9/7)
Models vertex :math:`A` and the internal/external touchpoint harmonic conjugates along line :math:`AI I_A` for the incircle and :math:`A`-excircle.
Centers of Similitude: Excircles — Part 2 (006)
Derives :math:`|AI| = d\frac{r}{R-r}` and :math:`|AI_A| = d\frac{R}{R-r}` (where :math:`R = r_a` is the exradius and :math:`d = |II_A|`).
Inverse Stewart Problem: Finding k for Given Cevian Length d (007)
Rearranges Stewart's theorem into the quadratic :math:`c^2 k^2 - (c^2+a^2-b^2)k + (a^2-d^2) = 0`.
Worked Quadratic Example (a, b, c, d) = (7, 5, 10, 4) (008)
Solves for the two base division ratios :math:`k = 0.613` and :math:`k = 0.147` at which a cevian of length :math:`d=4` meets base :math:`c=10`.
Discriminant & Minimum Cevian Length d_min = h_c (009)
Shows that the quadratic discriminant vanishes precisely when :math:`d = d_{\min} = h_c \approx 3.25` (the perpendicular altitude).

topics.title: Vesica Piscis and Acute-Obtuse Probability
topics.subtitle: Locus of Longest-Side Triangles, Semicircle Partition, and Exact Area Ratio 3 pi / (5 pi - 6 sqrt(3))
topics.enunciation: When segment AB of length c is the longest side of triangle ABC, vertex C lies inside the vesica piscis of area c^2 (4 pi - 3 sqrt(3))/6; the semicircle of diameter AB partitions each quadrant of area c^2 (4 pi - 3 sqrt(3))/24 into an obtuse region (O) = c^2 pi / 16 and an acute region (A) = c^2 (5 pi - 6 sqrt(3))/48, giving an exact obtuse-to-acute probability ratio (O)/(A) = 3 pi / (5 pi - 6 sqrt(3)) approx 1.773.
synthesis: Titled *Notes on the locus of points C such that c = |AB| is the longest side* (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), this three-folio jewel connects :person:`Euclid`'s Opening Proposition :ref:`I.1` (the :term:`vesica piscis` formed by :g:`c_left` and :g:`c_right` of radius :math:`c`) with :ref:`III.31` (:person:`Thales`'s semicircle :g:`c_semi` on diameter :g:`A` :g:`B` of radius :math:`c/2`). Because :math:`|AC| \le c` and :math:`|BC| \le c`, any triangle with longest side :math:`c` has vertex :g:`C` inside the vesica piscis; by fourfold symmetry, Seelig analyzes a single upper-half quadrant of total area :math:`(O) + (A) = c^2\left(\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\right)`.

Inside the Thales quarter-disk of radius :math:`c/2`, the angle at :g:`C` is obtuse (:math:`\gamma > 90^\circ`), giving obtuse area :math:`(O) = \frac{1}{4}\pi(c/2)^2 = c^2\frac{\pi}{16}`. Subtracting :math:`(O)` from the quarter-vesica leaves the acute region :math:`(A) = c^2\frac{5\pi - 6\sqrt{3}}{48}`. Dividing the two yields the exact geometric probability ratio :math:`\frac{(O)}{(A)} = \frac{3\pi}{5\pi - 6\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.7731` (63.94% obtuse vs. 36.06% acute)—confirming why random triangles in the ``Monte Carlo`` spreadsheet are predominantly obtuse!
equations: (O) + (A) = c^2\left(\frac{\pi}{6} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\right) = c^2\frac{4\pi - 3\sqrt{3}}{24}, \qquad (O) = \frac{1}{4}\pi\left(\frac{c}{2}\right)^2 = c^2\frac{\pi}{16}
(A) = c^2\frac{5\pi - 6\sqrt{3}}{48}, \qquad \frac{(O)}{(A)} = \frac{3\pi}{5\pi - 6\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.7731
folio_summaries: Locus of Longest-Side Triangles in the Vesica Piscis (001)
Identifies the region where :math:`|AC| \le c` and :math:`|BC| \le c` with the vesica piscis on :math:`AB` and computes the quarter-vesica area :math:`c^2\frac{4\pi-3\sqrt{3}}{24}`.
Thales Semicircle Partition into Obtuse (O) & Acute (A) Regions (002)
Uses the semicircle of radius :math:`c/2` on diameter :math:`AB` to separate obtuse triangles :math:`(O) = c^2\pi/16` from acute triangles :math:`(A) = c^2\frac{5\pi-6\sqrt{3}}{48}`.
Exact Obtuse-to-Acute Probability Ratio (003)
Evaluates :math:`(O)/(A) = \frac{3\pi}{5\pi-6\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.773` and compares with the empirical counts in the Monte Carlo spreadsheet.

topics.title: Altitudes, Mitchell's Reciprocal Heron Formula, and the Symphonic Theorem
topics.subtitle: The Sweet Theorem (h = ab/c), Reciprocal Altitude Area Formula, and Six Orthocenter Identities
topics.enunciation: Given the three altitudes h_A, h_B, h_C of triangle ABC with reciprocal semiperimeter H = (h_A^{-1} + h_B^{-1} + h_C^{-1})/2, Mitchell's reciprocal Heron formula states K^{-1} = 4 sqrt(H (H - h_A^{-1})(H - h_B^{-1})(H - h_C^{-1})), and a triangle is right-angled at C if and only if h_A^{-2} + h_B^{-2} = h_C^{-2} (the Symphonic Theorem).
synthesis: Across four folios (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig synthesizes the metric laws of the three :term:`altitude` segments :g:`h_a`, :g:`h_b`, :g:`h_c`. Folio 1 (*Altitude of a Right Triangle (the sweet theorem)*) derives :math:`h = ab/c` and the Inverse Pythagorean Theorem :math:`h^{-2} = a^{-2} + b^{-2}`. Folios 2–3 record :person:`Mitchell`'s (2005) reciprocal :term:`Heron's formula` (:cite:`Mitchell2005`): defining :math:`H = \frac{1}{2}(h_A^{-1}+h_B^{-1}+h_C^{-1})`, the reciprocal area is :math:`K^{-1} = 4\sqrt{H(H-h_A^{-1})(H-h_B^{-1})(H-h_C^{-1})}`, which immediately recovers each side via :math:`a = 2K/h_A`. Seelig also names the *Symphonic Theorem*: since :math:`h_A = b, h_B = a, h_C = ab/c` in a right triangle, the three altitudes satisfy :math:`h_A^{-2} + h_B^{-2} = h_C^{-2}`.

Folio 4 compiles six classical :term:`orthocenter` identities in :term:`Conway triangle notation`, including the sum of upper altitude segments :math:`t_A + t_B + t_C = |AH| + |BH| + |CH| = 2(r + R)` and the altitude-chord product :math:`|AH|\cdot|HH_A| = |BH|\cdot|HH_B| = |CH|\cdot|HH_C|`.
equations: \frac{1}{h_A^2} + \frac{1}{h_B^2} = \frac{1}{h_C^2} \quad (\gamma = 90^\circ), \qquad |AH| + |BH| + |CH| = 2(r + R)

The Symphonic Theorem & Altitude Ratios (altitudes-002)
States the Symphonic Theorem :math:`h_A^{-2} + h_B^{-2} = h_C^{-2}` for right triangles and relates :math:`h_A : h_B : h_C = a^{-1} : b^{-1} : c^{-1}`.
Six Orthocenter Segment Identities in Conway Notation (altitudes-003)
Records :math:`t_A + t_B + t_C = 2(r+R)` and five companion identities for the upper and lower orthocenter segments.

topics.title: Apollonian Circles and the Problem of Apollonius
topics.subtitle: Locus |PA|/|PB| = k, Integer Mean Triples, Power of a Point, and Dörrie's 8-Circle Tangency Table
topics.enunciation: The locus of points P with distance ratio |PA| / |PB| = k > 1 (where |AB| = d) is the Apollonian circle of radius R = d k / (k^2 - 1) centered at distance M' = d / (k^2 - 1) beyond B, cutting line AB at the internal and external harmonic conjugates C and D such that |A T'|^2 = |AC| |AD| = |AB| |A M'|.
synthesis: Dated February 7, 2014 (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig's nine-folio treatise on the :term:`Apollonian circles` combines the locus definition :math:`|PA|/|PB| = k` (Folios 1–8) with the classic *Problem of :person:`Apollonius`* (Folio 9, citing :person:`Dorrie`'s *100 Great Problems of Elementary Mathematics*, Problem #32, pp. 154–160, :cite:`Dorrie1965`). Given :math:`|AB| = d`, the internal and external bisectors of :math:`\angle APB` meet :math:`AB` at the :term:`harmonic conjugate` points :g:`C` and :g:`D` (:person:`Euclid` *Elements* :ref:`VI.3`), giving diameter endpoints separated by :math:`2R = \frac{2dk}{k^2-1}` and center :g:`M_p` at :math:`M' = \frac{d}{k^2-1}` from :g:`B`.

Across Folios 4–7, Seelig proves the power-of-a-point tangent identity :math:`|AT'|^2 = |AC|\cdot|AD| = |AB|\cdot|AM'|` and asks when two numbers :math:`m, n` yield simultaneous integer arithmetic, geometric, and harmonic means—finding the parametric solution :math:`m = 36, n = 324 \implies A = 180, G = 108, H = 64.8` (or scaled by 5 for all integers). Folio 9 classifies all :math:`2^3 = 8` Apollonian tangent circles to three given circles by their internal (``I``) or external (``X``) tangency signatures.
equations: \frac{|PA|}{|PB|} = k \implies M' = \frac{d}{k^2 - 1}, \qquad R = \frac{d k}{k^2 - 1}, \qquad R^2 - {M'}^2 = \frac{d^2}{k^2 - 1}
|A T'|^2 = |AC|\cdot|AD| = |AB|\cdot|A M'| = d(d + M') = \frac{d^2 k^2}{k^2 - 1}
folio_summaries: Apollonian Circle Center M' & Radius R (apollonian-001, FWS 2/7/2014)
Derives :math:`|BC| = d/(k+1), |BD| = d/(k-1), M' = d/(k^2-1)`, and :math:`R = dk/(k^2-1)` for the locus :math:`|PA|/|PB| = k`.
Cartesian Equation Completion of the Square (apollonian-002)
Expands :math:`(x+d)^2 + y^2 = k^2(x^2+y^2)` and completes the square to confirm center :math:`(d/(k^2-1), 0)` and radius :math:`dk/(k^2-1)`.
Angle Bisector Proof via Euclid VI.3 (apollonian-003)
Shows that the internal and external bisectors of :math:`\angle APB` meet :math:`AB` at fixed harmonic points :math:`C, D` with :math:`\angle CPD = 90^\circ`.
Power of Point A & Tangent Length |AT'| (apollonian-004)
Proves :math:`|AT'|^2 = |AC|\cdot|AD| = |AB|\cdot|AM'|` for the tangent :math:`AT'` from :math:`A` to the Apollonian circle.
Orthogonal Circle of Inversion Centered at A or B (apollonian-005)
Shows that the circle centered at :math:`A` of radius :math:`|AT'| = dk/\sqrt{k^2-1}` is orthogonal to the Apollonian circle.
Arithmetic, Geometric & Harmonic Means on Segment AD (apollonian-006)
Identifies :math:`|AB|, |AC|, |AD|, |AM'|` with the classical Pythagorean means.
Integer Mean Search: m = 36, n = 324 (apollonian-007)
Solves for integer pairs :math:`(m,n)` having integer arithmetic mean :math:`A = 180` and geometric mean :math:`G = 108`.
Coaxial Family of Apollonian Circles for Varying k (apollonian-008)
Plots the nested Apollonian circles around limiting points :math:`A` and :math:`B` with the perpendicular bisector as the :math:`k=1` radical axis.
Problem of Apollonius — Dörrie's 8-Circle I/X Tangency Table (apollonius-2-001)
Cites Heinrich Dörrie (#32, pp. 154–160) and tabulates all 8 solution circles by their internal (``I``) and external (``X``) tangency states to three given circles.

topics.title: Homogeneous Barycentric Coordinates
topics.subtitle: Classical Center Catalog X(1)–X(8), Sidelength Polynomials for X(5), and 5-6-7 Evaluations
topics.enunciation: Every triangle center X(n) has homogeneous barycentric coordinates (u : v : w) normalizable to absolute weights lambda_A + lambda_B + lambda_C = 1 such that X = lambda_A A + lambda_B B + lambda_C C; for the nine-point center N = X(5), lambda_A = 1/4 + (b^2 - c^2)(a^2 - (b^2 + c^2)) / (32 K^2).
synthesis: Spanning 15 folios (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig's master treatise on :term:`homogeneous barycentric coordinates` (HBC) bridges classical synthetic geometry, :person:`Kimberling`'s *Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers* (:cite:`KimberlingETC`), and programmable calculator/spreadsheet computation. Folios 1–6 (`bari-centers-001`–`006`) tabulate the unnormalized homogeneous coordinates :math:`(u:v:w)`, normalizing sums :math:`\Sigma = u+v+w`, and exact numerical evaluations on the canonical :math:`(5,6,7)` triangle for eight fundamental centers: :term:`incenter` :g:`I` :math:`= X(1) = (a:b:c)`, :term:`centroid` :g:`G` :math:`= X(2) = (1:1:1)`, :term:`circumcenter` :g:`O` :math:`= X(3) = (a^2 S_A : b^2 S_B : c^2 S_C)`, :term:`orthocenter` :g:`H` :math:`= X(4) = (S_B S_C : S_C S_A : S_A S_B)`, nine-point center :g:`N` :math:`= X(5)`, :term:`symmedian point` :math:`K = X(6) = (a^2:b^2:c^2)`, :term:`Gergonne point` :math:`Ge = X(7)`, and :term:`Nagel point` :math:`Na = X(8) = (s-a:s-b:s-c)`.

In Folios 7–15 (`homogenus-barycentric-co001`–`009`, dated `FWS 2014/9/14`), Seelig derives two explicit forms for the normalized barycentric coordinates of the nine-point center :g:`N` (:ref:`X(5)`): Form I (trigonometric, :math:`u = a\cos(\beta - \gamma)`) and Form II (purely polynomial in the side lengths: :math:`\lambda_A = W + \frac{P^2/a^2 + a^4}{D}` with :math:`D = 4U - 2S_4 = 16K^2`), verifying Form II on the :math:`(3,4,5)` right triangle :math:`(\frac{1}{4} : \frac{1}{4} : \frac{1}{2})`, the :math:`(5,6,7)` acute triangle :math:`(0.28299 : 0.30208 : 0.41493)`, and a compass drawing of the :math:`(7,8,9)` nine-point circle (:math:`R_N = \frac{21}{20}\sqrt{5}`).
equations: P = \lambda_A A + \lambda_B B + \lambda_C C \qquad (\lambda_A + \lambda_B + \lambda_C = 1), \qquad \lambda_A = \frac{u}{u + v + w} = \frac{[PBC]}{[ABC]}
X(1) = (a : b : c),\quad X(2) = (1 : 1 : 1),\quad X(3) = (a^2 S_A : b^2 S_B : c^2 S_C),\quad X(4) = (S_B S_C : S_C S_A : S_A S_B),\quad X(6) = (a^2 : b^2 : c^2)
folio_summaries: Homogeneous Barycentric Coordinates — Area & Mass Interpretation (bari-centers-001)
Defines :math:`\lambda_A = [PBC]/[ABC], \lambda_B = [PCA]/[ABC], \lambda_C = [PAB]/[ABC]` with :math:`\lambda_A + \lambda_B + \lambda_C = 1`.
Master Barycentric Catalog: X(1), X(2), X(3), X(4) (bari-centers-002)
Tabulates algebraic and Conway-notation barycentric weights for the incenter :math:`I`, centroid :math:`G`, circumcenter :math:`O`, and orthocenter :math:`H`.
Master Barycentric Catalog: X(5), X(6), X(7), X(8) (bari-centers-003)
Tabulates barycentric weights for the nine-point center :math:`N`, symmedian point :math:`K`, Gergonne point :math:`G_e`, and Nagel point :math:`N_a`.
Canonical (5, 6, 7) Barycentric Evaluation Table — Part 1 (bari-centers-004)
Evaluates exact rational and decimal normalized barycentric coordinates of :math:`I, G, O, H` on the :math:`(5,6,7)` triangle.
Canonical (5, 6, 7) Barycentric Evaluation Table — Part 2 (bari-centers-005)
Evaluates normalized barycentric and Cartesian coordinates of :math:`N, K, G_e, N_a` on the :math:`(5,6,7)` triangle.
Euler Line Barycentric Combinations (bari-centers-006)
Verifies :math:`G = \frac{2}{3}O + \frac{1}{3}H` and :math:`N = \frac{1}{2}O + \frac{1}{2}H` directly on the normalized barycentric triples.
Nine-Point Center N = X(5) — Form I & Form II (co001, FWS 2014/9/14)
States Form I (:math:`a\cos(\beta-\gamma)`) and derives Form II (:math:`\lambda_A = W + \frac{P^2/a^2 + a^4}{D}` with :math:`D = 4U - 2S_4`) purely in terms of side lengths :math:`a, b, c`.
Algebraic Reduction of Form II (co002)
Expands the symmetric polynomials :math:`P = abc, U = a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2, S_4 = a^4+b^4+c^4` and proves :math:`\lambda_A + \lambda_B + \lambda_C = 1`.
Verification of Form II on the (3, 4, 5) Right Triangle (co003)
Evaluates Form II at :math:`(a,b,c) = (3,4,5)` to obtain :math:`(\lambda_A, \lambda_B, \lambda_C) = (1/4, 1/4, 1/2)`.
Verification of Form II on the (5, 6, 7) Triangle (co004)
Evaluates Form II at :math:`(a,b,c) = (5,6,7)` to obtain :math:`(\lambda_A, \lambda_B, \lambda_C) = (163/576, 174/576, 239/576) \approx (0.28299, 0.30208, 0.41493)`.
Nine-Point Circle of the (7, 8, 9) Triangle — Calculations (co005)
Computes :math:`N, R = \frac{21\sqrt{5}}{10}`, and :math:`R_N = \frac{21\sqrt{5}}{20}` for the :math:`(7,8,9)` acute triangle.

topics.title: Geometric Half-Angle Trigonometry
topics.subtitle: Unit Semicircle Chord Proof of cos^2(theta/2) and sin^2(theta/2)
topics.enunciation: In a unit semicircle of radius R = 1 and diameter AB = 2, a point P at central angle theta has altitude sin(theta), base projections 1 + cos(theta) and 1 - cos(theta), and chord |AP| = 2 cos(theta/2) = sqrt(2 + 2 cos(theta)), giving cos^2(theta/2) = (1 + cos(theta))/2 and sin^2(theta/2) = (1 - cos(theta))/2.
synthesis: In this elegant single-folio geometric proof (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), Seelig derives the half-angle identities for :math:`\cos^2(\theta/2)` and :math:`\sin^2(\theta/2)` directly from a unit semicircle (:math:`R = 1`, diameter :math:`|AB| = 2`) without algebraic angle-addition expansion. Dropping the altitude :math:`|PH| = \sin\theta` from :g:`P` to diameter :g:`A` :g:`B` divides the diameter into :math:`|AH| = 1 + \cos\theta` and :math:`|HB| = 1 - \cos\theta`.

By the inscribed angle theorem (:person:`Euclid` *Elements* :ref:`III.20`), the angle at :g:`A` is :math:`\theta/2`, so the chord :g:`s_ap` has length :math:`2x = 2\cos(\theta/2)`. Applying the Pythagorean theorem (:ref:`I.47`) to right triangle :math:`\triangle AHP` gives :math:`(2x)^2 = \sin^2\theta + (1 + \cos\theta)^2 = 2 + 2\cos\theta`, whence :math:`x^2 = \cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\cos\theta` and :math:`\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2}\cos\theta`.
equations: (2 x)^2 = \sin^2\theta + (1 + \cos\theta)^2 = 2 + 2\cos\theta \implies \cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1 + \cos\theta}{2}
\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} = 1 - \cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{2}, \qquad \tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{\sin\theta}{1 + \cos\theta}
folio_summaries: Unit Semicircle Proof of Half-Angle Identities

Constructs right triangle :math:`AHP` inside a unit semicircle (:math:`R=1, |AH|=1+\cos\theta, |PH|=\sin\theta, |AP|=2\cos(\theta/2)`) to prove :math:`\cos^2(\theta/2) = \frac{1}{2}(1+\cos\theta)` and :math:`\sin^2(\theta/2) = \frac{1}{2}(1-\cos\theta)`.

.. math::

   (2 x)^2 = \sin^2\theta + (1 + \cos\theta)^2 = 2 + 2\cos\theta \implies \cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{1 + \cos\theta}{2}

topics.title: HP-35s Triangle Program and Coordinate Scripts
topics.subtitle: BARY 2 CAR and CAR 2 BARY Matrix Routines, Register Map A–Z, and 5-6-7 Verification
topics.enunciation: In the canonical frame A = (0, 0), B = (M, 0), C = (I, J), the forward and inverse barycentric-Cartesian transformations BARY 2 CAR and CAR 2 BARY are given by P = M U + I V, Q = J V and V = Q / J, U = (P - I V) / M, T = 1 - (U + V).
synthesis: Dated September 10, 2014 with ``LAST EDIT May 7, 2015`` (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), these two folios document Seelig's ``HP-35s [T] [Triangle]`` calculator program specification. Placing :g:`A` at :math:`(0,0)`, :g:`B` at :math:`(M,0)`, and :g:`C` at :math:`(I,J)`, the program maps normalized :term:`homogeneous barycentric coordinates` :math:`(T, U, V) = (\lambda_A, \lambda_B, \lambda_C)` to Cartesian coordinates :math:`(P, Q) = (x, y)` via the upper-triangular routine ``BARY 2 CAR``: :math:`P = MU + IV, Q = JV`.

Conversely, the inverse routine ``CAR 2 BARY`` recovers the barycentric weights in three register operations: :math:`V = Q/J`, :math:`U = (P - IV)/M`, and :math:`T = 1 - (U + V)`. Folio 2 records the complete ``A``–``Z`` memory register map of the HP-35s alongside a worked validation on the canonical :math:`(5,6,7)` triangle.
equations: \text{BARY 2 CAR:}\quad \begin{bmatrix} P \\ Q \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} M & I \\ 0 & J \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} U \\ V \end{bmatrix}, \qquad T + U + V = 1
\text{CAR 2 BARY:}\quad V = \frac{Q}{J}, \qquad U = \frac{P - I V}{M}, \qquad T = 1 - (U + V)
folio_summaries: HP-35s [T] [Triangle] Program Specification (FWS Sept. 10, 2014 / May 7, 2015)

topics.title: Compass Constructions and Angle-to-Side Triangle Reconstruction
topics.subtitle: Vesica-Square Drawings and Reconstructing (a, b, c) from Interior Angles Under Scale Normalization
topics.enunciation: Given the three interior angles (alpha, beta, gamma) of a triangle normalized to unit area K = 1 (so s = 1/r), the Conway intouch segments x = s - a = r cot(alpha/2), y = s - b = r cot(beta/2), and z = s - c = r cot(gamma/2) determine the side lengths a = y + z, b = z + x, and c = x + y = 2 s - (a + b).
synthesis: Closing the 55-topic archive (:cite:`SeeligNotebooks`), this five-folio folder pairs two pure compass-and-straightedge drawings (`drawings-001`–`002`, showing overlapping circles, a :term:`vesica piscis`, and an inscribed square with perpendicular axes) with a three-page analytic study (`misc-2-001`–`003`) on reconstructing a triangle's side lengths :math:`(a,b,c)` and vertex coordinates :math:`(A,B,C)` from its interior angles :math:`(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)` under three alternative scale normalizations.

Under the unit-area normalization :math:`K = r s = 1` (so :math:`s = 1/r`), Seelig expresses the :term:`Conway triangle notation` intouch segments via the half-angle cotangents :math:`x = s - a = r\cot(\alpha/2)`, :math:`y = s - b = r\cot(\beta/2)`, and :math:`z = s - c = r\cot(\gamma/2)`, recovering :math:`c = (s-a) + (s-b) = 2s - (a+b)` and :math:`r^2 = \frac{1}{\cot(\alpha/2) + \cot(\beta/2) + \cot(\gamma/2)}`.
equations: s - a = r\cot\frac{\alpha}{2}, \qquad s - b = r\cot\frac{\beta}{2}, \qquad s - c = r\cot\frac{\gamma}{2}
K = r s = 1 \implies s = \frac{1}{r}, \qquad c = (s - a) + (s - b) = 2 s - (a + b)
folio_summaries: Compass Construction — Vesica Piscis & Orthogonal Axes (drawings-001)
Full-page compass and straightedge construction of a vesica piscis, perpendicular bisector, and inscribed circles.
Compass Construction — Inscribed Square & Diagonal Grid (drawings-002)
Compass construction of a circle, orthogonal diameters, and inscribed square with auxiliary secant lines.
Reconstructing a Triangle from Angles (alpha, beta, gamma) — Assumption Sets (misc-2-001)

Sets up the problem of determining :math:`(a,b,c)` and vertex coordinates :math:`(A,B,C)` from :math:`(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)` under three scale normalizations (:math:`c=1`, :math:`R=1`, or :math:`K=1`).
Unit-Area Normalization K = 1 & Intouch Cotangents (misc-2-002)
Uses :math:`K = rs = 1 \implies s = 1/r` and :math:`s - a = r\cot(\alpha/2), s - b = r\cot(\beta/2)` to solve for :math:`r, s`, and :math:`(a,b,c)`.
Side Recovery c = 2s - (a + b) & Vertex Coordinates (misc-2-003)
Recovers :math:`c = (s-a)+(s-b) = 2s-(a+b)` and writes the resulting Cartesian coordinates of :math:`A, B, C`.
